title: lockstep-requant-deconv-path: adaptive lock-step requantizer + deconv kernel path to reduce dequant hops
author: Samira Patel
release_notes: Introduces an adaptive lock-step requantizer that fuses dequant->compute->requant cycles for attention and FFN kernels, plus KV-cache alignment to avoid extra format conversions. Provides microbench harness and perf baselines. No public API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed repeated dequant->compute->requant cycles in the attention/FFN hot paths when serving mixed-precision INT8/FP8 model variants. These extra conversions were adding significant per-token latency for short-sequence workloads and prevented continuous batching from coalescing microbatches efficiently. This PR implements an adaptive lock-step requantizer that fuses dequant and requant operations around the core compute kernels (including a leaning deconv-style microkernel for weight layout transforms), aligns KV cache formats to the fused path to avoid format shuffles, and exposes a scheduler hint that prefers lockstep-compatible batches to the continuous batching coordinator.

What this PR changes (single string): Adds lockstep_requant operator and matching microkernel implementations for INT8 and FP8 pathways; implements kv_cache alignment and format tag so cached keys/values are stored in the fused-friendly layout; adds a deconv-style fused kernel (deconv_fused_int8.cu) used for compact weight reordering when models are loaded or when a fallback migration is triggered; exposes a small scheduling hint in batching_hints.cc so the continuous batcher will coalesce requests with compatible quant meta; introduces perf harness and baseline artifacts; documents the new path and migration instructions.

Checklist: - [x] Core lock-step requant operator implemented and unit-tested - [x] Fused deconv microkernel for layout transform implemented (CUDA) - [x] KV cache format alignment implemented and migration strategy added - [x] Scheduler hint implemented and wired into continuous batcher - [x] Perf harness + baselines included - [x] Docs describing migration and opt-in flag added - [x] No public API changes to Redwood API surface

Commits (high-level): - commit 1: initial lockstep operator API and tests - commit 2: CUDA deconv_fused_int8 microkernel and CPU reference - commit 3: KV cache alignment, migration path and cache tag metadata - commit 4: scheduler hint + continuous-batcher integration - commit 5: perf harness and docs - commit 6: follow-up micro-optimizations after perf run

Files changed (high level snippets): - runtime/quant/lockstep_requant.cpp: new operator with fallback path and adaptive thresholding based on observed scale drift - runtime/kernels/deconv_fused_int8.cu: custom fused copy+requant kernel optimized for contiguous weight blocks; contains small kernel loop unrolling and shared memory tiling tuned for 8-bit paths - runtime/kv/kv_alignment.cc: introduces KVFormatTag enum and conversion utilities; added a lightweight migration that converts in-place during cache warmup to avoid long stalls - runtime/scheduler/batching_hints.cc: adds prefer_lockstep_hint and small heuristics (sequence length, model variant compatibility)

Testing and perf: - Unit tests: added CPU reference tests and GPU integration tests covering numerical equivalence within tolerances for INT8/FP8 conversions. - Perf: microbench harness run on p4d-like cluster; results show median per-token latency improvement of 9-14% on short-sequence (<=64) chat workloads and a throughput improvement of ~7% for mixed small-batch scenarios. Baselines and raw outputs included in third_party/benchmarks/lockstep_baseline.json.

Compatibility and safety: The path is opt-in via runtime flag --quant-lockstep-enable=false by default for existing deployments. A migration path is provided: when enabled the KV cache tag will be written and existing cache entries are lazily converted on first access to avoid cold conversion spikes. Extensive numeric tolerancing checks are included to fallback to safe dequant->compute->requant if scale drift exceeds thresholds.

Review conversation (condensed single-string transcript): Darren Lee: "Nice direction; can you clarify the numerical tolerances and where the thresholds live? Also concerned about migration IO spikes." Samira Patel: "Thresholds are in lockstep_requant.h as MAX_SCALE_DRIFT (default 0.02) and are configurable via runtime config. Migration is lazy on access; added tests to ensure no synchronous cold path conversion. Details added to docs/perf/quant-paths.md." Priya Nand: "Please add a perf test for a pathological KV churn case and ensure we don't regress slow-path allocations." Samira Patel: "Added bench_lockstep_requant.py case simulating KV churn; allocator instrumentation shows no growth beyond steady-state—results attached." Marco Ruiz: "Code looks good, please squash the kernel micro-optimizations into one commit and add comments about shared memory sizing." Samira Patel: "Done; micro-optimizations squashed and comments added."

CI summary: initial run: build failed (lint error in docs) -> fixed; second run: unit-tests passed, integration GPU tests had a flaky kernel timeout -> increased kernel timeout and re-ran; final run: all checks green (build, unit-tests, integration-gpu, perf-smoke). Perf regression check reported a small warning (throughput variance +4%) but within acceptable thresholds for feature flag rollout.

Requested changes and responses (single string): - Request: document runtime flag and safe defaults. Response: added docs/perf/quant-paths.md and runtime flag default false. - Request: add KV churn perf test. Response: added bench_lockstep_requant.py and verified stability. - Request: squash micro-optimizations and comment shared mem assumptions. Response: done.

Decision and merge: After approvals from Darren Lee and Priya Nand and a green CI run, this PR was merged to main via squash merge on 2026-02-12. Merge notes: toggled feature flag off by default; ops run staged rollout with Canary enabled for a small % of traffic in Dedicated clusters before broader rollout.

Follow-ups: - ENG-2227: track telemetry for lockstep enablement and per-model latency deltas - ENG-2235: explore auto-enabled policy when model variant shows stable scale drift < threshold for 24h - PERF: upstream kernel autotuner to pick shared memory tile sizes based on device topology

One-line summary: Adds an opt-in adaptive lock-step requantization path with fused deconv microkernel and KV-cache alignment to cut dequant/requant hops and improve short-sequence latency and mixed-batch throughput.
notes: Feature flag disabled by default; staged canary rollout planned; perf baselines included in repo.
